title: Two solutions to the four-queens problem
summary: The left and right boards show the two valid solutions to the 4-queens problem.
context: The 4-queens problem asks us to place 4 queens on a 4×4 chessboard so that no two queens share a row, column, or diagonal. The boards in the figure have no numeric labels; for reference below, rows from top to bottom and columns from left to right are numbered starting at 1.
description: The table below gives the queen's column in each row from top to bottom on the left and right boards; all other squares are empty.

frames.title: Two solutions to the four-queens problem
frames.explanation: Both arrangements place one queen in every row and one in every column; for any pair of queens, the absolute difference between their row numbers differs from the absolute difference between their column numbers, so no two share a main diagonal or an antidiagonal either. The two boards are left-right mirror images of each other and form the complete solution set for 4 queens.
